protein_residue_explanation.baseline: Each candidate residue embedding is replaced by the mean embedding of the supplied protein sequence; non-candidate residues remain observed.
protein_residue_explanation.candidate_selection: Top 20 residues by mean drug-to-protein attention, averaged across real drug atoms.
protein_residue_explanation.stability_method: Spearman correlation between absolute SHAP rankings estimated from the first and second halves of sampled permutations.

validation.scope: Only the attention-screened candidate residues are perturbed; all other residues remain at their observed embeddings.

protein_residue_explanation.interpretation: Positive SHAP values raise the predicted model output relative to the stated embedding baseline; negative values lower it. These are model attributions, not experimentally verified binding effects.

drug_atom_explanation.interpretation: Positive contributions raise the model output relative to the zero-feature reference; negative contributions lower it. Importance is the sum of absolute feature attributions for each atom.

methodological_notes: Residue SHAP is estimated with sampled feature-order permutations over an attention-screened candidate set.
Deletion and sufficiency tests use the same candidate set and mean-embedding reference; they are not external biological validation.
Integrated Gradients uses a zero-valued atom-feature reference and trapezoidal integration.
Cross-attention indicates model attention allocation and must not be interpreted as a confirmed physical contact map.
